Below is a quick‑start guide that shows you how to use your **`delta_key`** (the API key you received from the Delta service) to pull the “comments” (or “reviews / feedback / notes”) that have been associated with the domain **apple.com**. > **TL;DR** > 1. Make a GET request to `https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/{domain}/comments` > 2. Pass your `delta_key` in the `Authorization` header (`Bearer `) > 3. Parse the JSON response --- ## 1. What you’ll need | Item | Why it matters | |------|----------------| | **Delta API key** (`delta_key`) | Authenticates you and authorises access to the domain‑comment data. | | **Domain name** (`apple.com`) | The target you want to query. | | **HTTP client** (curl, Postman, Python `requests`, etc.) | To send the request. | > **Tip:** If you’re not sure where to find your `delta_key`, check the “API Keys” section of your Delta dashboard or the email you received when you signed up. --- ## 2. Endpoint & Parameters | Element | Value | Notes | |---------|-------|-------| | **Base URL** | `https://api.delta.com` | (Replace with the correct base URL if your provider uses a different one.) | | **Endpoint** | `/v1/domains/{domain}/comments` | `{domain}` is a path parameter – e.g., `apple.com`. | | **Query parameters** | `?limit=100&offset=0` (optional) | Use `limit` to cap the number of comments returned, `offset` for pagination. | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | Required for authentication and content type. | **Full URL example** ``` https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments?limit=50 ``` --- ## 3. Sample Requests ### 3.1 Using `curl` ```bash curl -X GET \ "https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments?limit=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_DELTA_KEY" \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` ### 3.2 Using Python (`requests`) ```python import requests API_KEY = "YOUR_DELTA_KEY" DOMAIN = "apple.com" LIMIT = 50 url = f"https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/{DOMAIN}/comments?limit={LIMIT}" headers = { "Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}", "Accept": "application/json", } response = requests.get(url, headers=headers) if response.status_code == 200: comments = response.json() print(comments) # List of comment objects else: print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}") ``` ### 3.3 Using Postman 1. **Method**: GET 2. **URL**: `https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments?limit=50` 3. **Headers** - `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_DELTA_KEY` - `Accept: application/json` 4. Click **Send** and inspect the JSON body. --- ## 4. Typical Response Structure ```json { "domain": "apple.com", "total_comments": 237, "comments": [ { "id": "cmt_00123", "author": "Jane Doe", "timestamp": "2024-08-15T12:34:56Z", "text": "Great site, but the checkout process could be smoother.", "rating": 4 }, { "id": "cmt_00124", "author": "John Smith", "timestamp": "2024-08-14T09:21:00Z", "text": "Loved the new iPhone launch page!", "rating": 5 } // … more comments … ] } ``` > **Note:** The exact field names (`id`, `author`, `timestamp`, `text`, `rating`, etc.) may differ depending on the Delta API version. Check the official API docs for the precise schema. --- ## 5. Pagination If the domain has more comments than the `limit` you set, the response will include a `next` link or an `offset` value. Example: ```json { "next_offset": 50, "comments": [ ... ] } ``` To fetch the next batch: ```bash curl -X GET \ "https://api.delta.com/v1/domains/apple.com/comments?limit=50&offset=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_DELTA_KEY" \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` Repeat until `next_offset` is `null` or the returned array is empty. --- ## 6. Common Pitfalls & Troubleshooting | Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | **401 Unauthorized** | Wrong or missing API key | Verify the key, ensure it’s in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer `. | | **404 Not Found** | Wrong endpoint or domain typo | Double‑check the URL path and domain spelling. | | **429 Too Many Requests** | Rate limit exceeded | Add delays between requests or request a higher rate limit from Delta support. | | **500 Internal Server Error** | Temporary server issue | Retry after a few minutes; contact Delta support if persists. | --- ## 7. Next Steps 1. **Run the sample request** with your actual `delta_key`. 2. **Inspect the JSON** to confirm you’re receiving the expected comment data. 3. **Integrate** the call into your application (e.g., a backend service, a scheduled job, or a dashboard). 4. **Handle pagination** if you need all comments. 5. **Store** or display the comments as needed. --- ### Quick Checklist - [ ] Replace `YOUR_DELTA_KEY` with your real key. - [ ] Confirm the base URL (`https://api.delta.com`) matches your provider. - [ ] Test with a small `limit` (e.g., 10) to verify connectivity. - [ ] Handle errors gracefully in production code. Happy querying! If you hit any snags or need help parsing the response, just let me know.
